Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female with several days of dysuria and occasional lower abdominal cramping; no systemic symptoms. Clinical impression: uncomplicated lower UTI.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Stinging pain on urination for a few days; occasional lower abdominal cramp-like pain when urinating.
- Associated symptoms: Malodorous urine; small amount of blood in urine earlier today.
- Pertinent negatives: No increased urinary frequency noted; no back/flank pain; no fever; no nausea/vomiting; bowels normal (no diarrhea); no vaginal discharge.
- Gynecologic/sexual history: Sexually active with boyfriend (relationship ~2 months). Uses condoms. Last menstrual period “a couple of weeks ago” (doctor noted “three weeks” — conflict noted). Denies pregnancy but advised to test if concerned.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Medications: No regular medications. Tried over-the-counter bicarbonate a few days ago without relief (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Clindamycin — causes swelling.
- Family history: Denies known kidney/bladder/bowel/gastrointestinal conditions.
- Social history: College student living with friends. Non-smoker. Drinks alcohol socially on weekends.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Examination findings: Not documented. Physician stated would proceed to examination, but none recorded.

Impression:
- Uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).

Plan:
- Antibiotic: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim prescribed; instructions given as 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days. Exact agent and route not documented.
- Hydration: Increase oral fluids; cranberry juice may help symptomatically.
- Sexual activity: Avoid intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.
- Safety-net advice: Return/call if symptoms persist beyond the end of the week or if red flags develop (fever, back pain, feeling generally more unwell) due to concern for possible pyelonephritis.
- Pregnancy: Advised to perform a pregnancy test if any concern or if symptoms persist.
- Follow-up: Contact provider by end of the week if not improving.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - No vitals or physical exam documented.
  - No urinalysis or urine culture ordered/documented.
  - No pregnancy test performed.
  - No STI screening planned despite being sexually active and never previously screened.
  - Antibiotic details incomplete (exact agent, dose in mg, and route not fully documented).
  - Full medication reconciliation beyond current/OTC use not detailed (e.g., supplements).
● Internal conflicts:
  - Last menstrual period reported as “a couple of weeks ago”; doctor documented “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).
  - Brief initial ambiguity on fever (“think so”) later clarified to “no fever.”
● Transcript quality:
  - Minor audio interruptions and pauses; otherwise understandable.
